clues: This town lies in the north of the land, on the banks of the Sava. It rests at the south foot of a great hill slope just by the town.
This town has four clear times of year, each one set far from the rest. Spring, summer, fall, and winter all come in turn here each year.
In 1991 this land broke free and stood on its own as a state. The men who made its laws then named this town its chief town.
Every day at noon — and it has happened since 1877! — a cannon fires from a tower in the old town to mark midday.
Croatia is run from this town, where the work of state is done each day. More folk live here than in any other town in the land.
